success_patterns: Single-domain routing on refinement turns. Neighborhood on restaurants, and 'gym and pool' on filtered_hotels, each produced exactly load -> filter -> save for that one domain. No other domain's key was touched.

A load -> filter -> save refinement passes only the last message's new constraint. The neighborhood reply gave neighborhood=['Downtown St. Louis'] with no cuisine or vegetarian re-passed. The gym/pool reply gave gym_present and pool_present only. The save key was new (filtered_restaurants, final_hotels).

Hotel first-search after dates arrive with restaurants already cached. search_hotels was called alone with every literal value (city from turn 1, both dates as written, num_rooms=3, num_people=5), saved as 'hotels', and restaurants were not re-searched.

A near-miss: for 'a kid-friendly pool and breakfast included' the agent added has_kids_club=True on top of pool_present and breakfast_included. It still scored, but the extra param was a false positive. 'Kid-friendly' or 'family-friendly' wording leaked into an amenity flag even though Rules 2 and 10 already forbid it.

patch.reasoning: Nearly every success was already covered by the existing rules (one-domain routing, minimal filters, first-search with literal values, final_* key naming). The only gap with direct evidence is amenity mapping. In trajectory 4 the agent turned the descriptive 'kid-friendly' into has_kids_club, and 'family-friendly' from turn 1 probably fed that. The rule against it sits in Rules 2 and 10, away from the amenity mapping table the agent looks up when writing kwargs. I fold the guard into the existing 'kids club' mapping entry rather than adding another example or rule, so the skill does not grow by accretion.

edits.content: 'kids club' -> has_kids_club=True (only when the user literally says 'kids club'; 'kid-friendly', 'family-friendly' or 'family vacation' never set it, so 'kid-friendly pool' -> pool_present=True only).
